service.name: Musician for a proposal or a surprise song
service.serviceType: A musician or duo for a marriage proposal, a surprise song at a birthday or anniversary dinner, or a short set at a small private moment
service.description: A guitarist, a singer or a duo playing one song or a short set at a marriage proposal, a surprise at a birthday or anniversary dinner, or a small private moment, in Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain towns, booked at a minimum and planned to the minute with the person arranging it.

faqs.q: Can I hire a musician for just one song?
faqs.a: Yes. A proposal, a surprise at a birthday dinner, an anniversary, a song at a graveside: one song is a real booking here, and we plan it as carefully as a four-hour evening. There is a booking minimum, because the musician's whole evening goes to being in the right place at the right minute, and it is quoted for the date when you send it. Nothing about the size of the moment makes it less worth doing.

faqs.q: How does a proposal with a musician work?
faqs.a: You tell us the place, the time, the song and who is in on it. The musician is set up early, usually as background music nobody looks at twice, plays a few songs so the setup reads as part of the place, and lands your song on your cue. A hand signal, a text, or a friend's nod. After the yes, the set keeps going while the two of you get your breath back, or stops so the moment is yours.

A solo guitarist, a singer with a guitar, or a Spanish guitarist, depending on the song and the place. Instrumental guitar suits a song you want to recognise without a voice saying the words for you; a singer suits a song whose words are the point. A duo, upright bass and guitar, suits a restaurant or a home where a little more sound is wanted.

faqs.q: Can a musician sing happy birthday at a dinner, or play our wedding song at an anniversary?
faqs.a: Yes, and both are the same booking as a proposal: a short set at conversation volume, one song placed on cue, and a musician who was in the restaurant before the guest of honour arrived. Tell us the song and who it's for and the set is built around them.

faqs.q: Do restaurants and public places allow it?
faqs.a: Most restaurants say yes when asked in advance, and we ask, so the manager knows a musician is coming and where the small case goes. A park, a trailhead or a rooftop is a different question, sometimes a permit and sometimes a battery-powered system, and we plan that with you. What we never do is surprise the venue.

faqs.q: What does a one-song booking cost?
faqs.a: It carries a booking minimum, because the musician's evening goes to being in exactly the right place at exactly the right time, and the minimum is quoted for the date when you send it. We publish no prices of our own. What a short live-music booking runs across this market is set out, sourced, in the cost guide.
